```{r}
df_register <- df_register %>% rename(age_group = dob)

# Trim whitespace and standardise case, in case of "35 - 44" vs "35-44"
clean <- function(x) tolower(trimws(gsub("\\s*-\\s*", "-", x)))
for (v in c("sex", "citizenship", "marital_status", "age_group")) {
  df_X[[v]]        <- clean(df_X[[v]])
  df_register[[v]] <- clean(df_register[[v]])
}
df_register <- df_register %>%
  mutate(evote = as.integer(last_voted == 1))

df_register

```

Deterministic methods:

```{r}
library(dplyr)

keys <- c("sex", "citizenship", "marital_status", "age_group", "last_voted","evote")

# --- Linkage (unchanged) -----------------------------------------------------
cand <- df_X %>%
  select(X_id = X, all_of(keys)) %>%
  inner_join(df_register %>% select(reg_id = X, name, zip, all_of(keys)),
             by = keys, relationship = "many-to-many")

n_cand <- cand %>% count(X_id, name = "n_candidates")

df_X2 <- df_X %>%
  left_join(n_cand, by = c("X" = "X_id")) %>%
  mutate(n_candidates = coalesce(n_candidates, 0L))

unique_matches <- cand %>%
  semi_join(filter(n_cand, n_candidates == 1), by = "X_id")

# --- Context for the numbers -------------------------------------------------
N     <- nrow(df_X2)
N_reg <- nrow(df_register)
  
df_X2 <- df_X2 %>%
  mutate(match_status = case_when(
    n_candidates == 0 ~ "1. No match",
    n_candidates == 1 ~ "2. Unique match",
    TRUE              ~ "3. Ambiguous"
  ))

# 1) Overall outcome
df_X2 %>%
  count(match_status) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / N, 1),
         meaning = case_when(
           match_status == "1. No match"     ~ "Nobody in the register fits all 5 keys (not in register, or an attribute differs)",
           match_status == "2. Unique match" ~ "Exactly one register person fits: re-identified",
           TRUE                              ~ "Several people fit: you can only narrow it down"
         ))

# 2) How ambiguous are the ambiguous ones? (size of the "anonymity set")
df_X2 %>%
  filter(n_candidates > 1) %>%
  summarise(
    respondents = n(),
    min    = min(n_candidates),
    median = median(n_candidates),
    mean   = round(mean(n_candidates), 1),
    p90    = quantile(n_candidates, 0.9),
    max    = max(n_candidates)
  )

# 3) Risk bands: fewer candidates = easier to re-identify
df_X2 %>%
  filter(n_candidates > 0) %>%
  mutate(risk_band = cut(n_candidates,
                         breaks = c(0, 1, 5, 20, Inf),
                         labels = c("1 (unique)", "2-5 (high risk)",
                                    "6-20 (medium)", ">20 (low)"))) %>%
  count(risk_band) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))

# 4) Expected number of correct names if you guess randomly among candidates
exp_correct <- sum(1 / df_X2$n_candidates[df_X2$n_candidates > 0])
cat(sprintf(
  "\nRegister size: %d | Respondents: %d (%.1f%% of register)\n",
  N_reg, N, 100 * N / N_reg))
cat(sprintf(
  "Expected correct identifications by random guessing: %.1f of %d (%.1f%%)\n",
  exp_correct, N, 100 * exp_correct / N))
cat(sprintf(
  "Naive baseline (guessing any register person): %.2f of %d\n",
  N / N_reg * N, N))   # roughly N * (1 / N_reg)... see note below

# 5) Who is uniquely identified
unique_matches %>% select(X_id, reg_id, name, zip)
```
```{r}

# Sanity check: total candidate pairs should be 4,597
sum(df_X2$n_candidates)

# Uniquely linkable respondents with their sensitive attributes
identified <- unique_matches %>%
  select(X_id, reg_id, name, zip) %>%
  left_join(df_X %>% select(X, education, evote, party),
            by = c("X_id" = "X"))

# Collisions: two respondents linking to the same register person
identified %>% count(reg_id) %>% filter(n > 1)

identified %>% select(name, zip, party)
count(identified, party)
```


```{r}

risk <- df_X2 %>%
  mutate(
    guess_prob = ifelse(n_candidates > 0, 1 / n_candidates, 0),
    tier = case_when(
      n_candidates == 0  ~ "E: no strict match",
      n_candidates == 1  ~ "A: unique",
      n_candidates <= 5  ~ "B: 2-5 candidates",
      n_candidates <= 20 ~ "C: 6-20 candidates",
      TRUE               ~ "D: >20 candidates"
    )
  )

risk %>% group_by(tier) %>%
  summarise(respondents = n(), expected_correct = round(sum(guess_prob), 1))
```
```{r}
small <- cand %>%
  inner_join(df_X2 %>% select(X, n_candidates, party), by = c("X_id" = "X")) %>%
  filter(n_candidates %in% 2) %>%
  arrange(n_candidates, X_id)

# Long view: one row per respondent-candidate pair
small %>% select(X_id, n_candidates, party, reg_id, name, zip)

# Compact view: one row per respondent, candidates listed together
small_compact <- small %>%
  group_by(X_id, n_candidates, party) %>%
  summarise(candidates = paste0(name, " (", zip, ")", collapse = "; "),
            .groups = "drop")

small_compact
```
